| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | Publisher-level (Taylor & Francis Group) policy applies to Digital Creativity; no journal-specific AI page found. T&F: generative AI/LLM tools (e.g. ChatGPT) cannot be credited as author; permitted uses include idea generation/exploration, language/grammar polishing, LLM-enhanced literature search, and coding/script-writing assistance; prohibited for unverified content generation (e.g. abstracts, supplementary text) and for generating/manipulating research data, images, figures. Any AI use must be disclosed (tool name, version, purpose) in Methods/Acknowledgments. This is publisher-wide guidance (per Taylor & Francis Newsroom announcements), not confirmed as customized for this specific journal. |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes (publisher-level T&F policy) - authors may post/share their Author's Original Manuscript (preprint) at any time, including on preprint servers/repositories prior to and during submission; Accepted Manuscript can be self-archived after publication under green OA with an embargo. Journal is also hybrid Open Select (gold OA option available).

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Journal is publishing work engaging with AI/generative-AI and digital creative practice: 'Another kind of authenticity: the visual simulacra of artificial intelligence' (Vol 36 No 1, Feb 2025), 'A knotwork for alternative AI: pursuing community-centred and co-creative technological practices' (2025), alongside participatory/placemaking methodology pieces ('Co-creating future narratives: a participatory methodology for digital placemaking', Vol 37 No 2, Oct 2025) and craft/education pieces (e.g. 'Using artificial intelligence in craft education: crafting with text-to-image generative models', 2023). Core scope per about-page: visual arts, interaction design, physical computing/making, computational materials, textile/fashion design, film/animation, game design, music, dance, drama, architecture and urban design.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** practice-based / practice-led research, participatory and co-design methodology, critical/theoretical essays on digital media and creative practice, case studies in interaction design, craft, game design, film/animation, scoping reviews (e.g. 'How to Enrich Digital Creativity? A Scoping Review', 2025)
